defaultScenario.title: Closed-Loop EV Battery Recycling & Hydrometallurgical Purity
defaultScenario.prompt: Identify emerging technology providers specializing in closed-loop hydrometallurgical or direct recycling of lithium-ion EV battery packs (NMC chemistries). Must achieve >95% recovery yield of battery-grade lithium carbonate/hydroxide with verified continuous pilot operations in EU or North America.
mustHaves: Granted or pending patent protection in EU/US

technologyCategories.name: Hydrometallurgy
technologyCategories.description: Chemical leaching and selective precipitation using organic or mild inorganic acids at moderate temperatures (<90°C).
technologyCategories.pros: High lithium recovery rate (>95%), low direct carbon emissions, flexible for mixed cathode chemistries.
technologyCategories.cons: Requires chemical reagent management and closed-loop wastewater recycling.

technologyCategories.name: Direct Cathode Recycling
technologyCategories.description: Relithiation and regeneration of cathode crystals without breaking down into constituent metal salts.
technologyCategories.pros: Preserves crystal morphology, lowest energy footprint, avoids expensive chemical precursors.
technologyCategories.cons: Sensitive to feed contamination; difficult to apply to heterogeneous aged battery scrap.

technologyCategories.name: Pyrometallurgical Smelting
technologyCategories.description: High-temperature thermal smelting (>1200°C) producing a cobalt-nickel alloy matte and slag.
technologyCategories.pros: Robust to battery format; requires minimal mechanical dismantling; established industrial footprint.
technologyCategories.cons: Burns off lithium and graphite into slag; high greenhouse gas emissions; poor circularity.

technologyCategories.name: Automated Robotic Disassembly
technologyCategories.description: Vision-guided robotic pack unscrewing, busbar desoldering, and cell sorting prior to chemical processing.
technologyCategories.pros: Eliminates dangerous manual high-voltage dismantling; reduces fire hazard during mechanical shredding.
technologyCategories.cons: High initial robotic capex; requires standardized pack CAD data across vehicle models.

startups.name: Circura Materials GmbH
startups.headline: Continuous Low-Temperature Hydrometallurgical Cathode Upcycling
startups.recommendation: Priority 1: Top Candidate for Joint Development Agreement (JDA) and physical assay validation.
startups.overview: Circura operates a continuous-flow 1,000 t/year operational hydrometallurgy pilot facility in Baden-Württemberg. Using proprietary citric-organic acid leaching at 65°C, they achieve >95.8% recovery of battery-grade lithium carbonate and >98% nickel/cobalt from aged EV black mass.
keyStrengths: Operating 1,000 t/yr continuous pilot verified by independent technical audit
Battery-grade lithium purity (99.6%) demonstrated on real-world automotive scrap
4 granted European and US patents with zero external IP encumbrances
Pre-commercial supply agreement with European Tier-1 battery pack integrator
keyRisks: Reagent regeneration supply chain requires long-term vendor qualification
Expansion to 10,000 t/yr commercial site requires local environmental zoning permits

comparisonMetrics.technologyMaturity: TRL 7 (Operational continuous pilot in Stuttgart, Germany)
comparisonMetrics.publications: 4 peer-reviewed journal papers (Eur. J. Sustainable Met. 2023-2024)
comparisonMetrics.commercialDeployment: Verified operational pilot facility (1,000 t/yr capacity)
comparisonMetrics.industrialPartnerships: 2 active industrial partnerships (Tier-1 Auto Consortium, Nordic Recycler)
comparisonMetrics.strategicVerdict: Shortlist #1: Immediate physical sample validation and JDA negotiations

findings.claim: Continuous hydrometallurgical pilot plant operating at 1,000 metric tons/year capacity in Stuttgart, Germany.
findings.source: State Industrial Environment Registry & Fraunhofer IPA Audit
findings.snippet: Facility inspection confirms continuous acid-leach pilot reactor operating at steady-state 1,000 t/a throughput processing NMC622 black mass.

findings.source: European Journal of Sustainable Metallurgy, Vol. 18, pp. 112-128
findings.snippet: Analytical ICP-MS assays confirm 95.8 ± 0.4% Li recovery with iron and aluminum contaminant concentrations below 10 ppm.

findings.claim: Assignee of 4 granted patents covering selective ultrasonic-assisted organic acid leaching without toxic chlorine emissions.
findings.source: European Patent Office (EPO) Register & USPTO Patent Public Search
findings.snippet: Patent EP3892011B1 granted with all 14 independent claims intact; no opposition proceedings filed.

findings.claim: Proprietary process reduces cradle-to-gate greenhouse gas emissions by 68% compared to pyrometallurgical smelting.
findings.snippet: Self-reported Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) conducted using internal baseline models; third-party ISO 14044 verification in progress.

findings.claim: Industrial scale commercial plant capex estimated at $42M with EBITDA positive return at 8,000 t/year utilization.
findings.snippet: Derived by cross-referencing Circura's published bill of materials, reactor residence times, and regional German utility tariffs.

findings.claim: Secured commercial supply off-take contract with a Tier-1 German automotive manufacturer for 3,000 t/year.
findings.snippet: Claims of a binding 3,000 t/year off-take agreement could not be confirmed in German corporate disclosures or OEM supply registers.

startups.name: HydraVolt Solutions Inc.
startups.headline: Ambient-Pressure Selective Solvent Extraction for Secondary Batteries
startups.recommendation: Priority 2: Qualified secondary partner; recommend technical due diligence on solvent degradation rates.
startups.overview: HydraVolt has pioneered ambient-pressure solvent extraction using specialized ionic liquids to selectively strip lithium and cobalt from shredded cell mass. They currently operate a 500 t/year demonstration facility in Hamilton, Ontario.
keyStrengths: Ambient pressure leaching reduces autoclave pressure vessel capex by 40%
Demonstrated 94.2% lithium extraction efficiency on NMC811 cells
Close geographic proximity to North American Great Lakes automotive manufacturing corridor
keyRisks: Ionic liquid solvent replenishment cost is high at commercial scale
Facility throughput (500 t/yr) is half the scale of Circura Materials

comparisonMetrics.technologyMaturity: TRL 6 (Continuous 500 t/yr demonstration plant in Ontario)
comparisonMetrics.industrialPartnerships: 1 joint evaluation agreement with North American mining partner
comparisonMetrics.strategicVerdict: Shortlist #2: Initiate pilot facility site audit and evaluate solvent unit economics

findings.claim: Achieves 94.2% lithium extraction without requiring high-pressure autoclaves.

startups.name: PyroLoop Technologies SAS
startups.headline: Industrial High-Throughput Clean Smelting & Metal Slag Recovery
startups.recommendation: Priority 3: Viable stopgap partner for high-volume smelting, but fails closed-loop lithium circularity goals.
startups.overview: PyroLoop is an established industrial operator with an active 15,000 t/year smelting plant near Lyon. While they achieve 99.1% recovery of Nickel and Cobalt with massive throughput, their thermal process burns off graphite and captures only 62% of lithium in insoluble slag.
keyStrengths: Highest operational throughput in cohort (15,000 t/year operational)
Proven ability to accept intact un-discharged modules without thermal runaway risk
Strong existing revenue and balance sheet stability
keyRisks: Substantially higher carbon footprint (>3.8 kg CO2e/kg metal recovered)
Inability to recover battery-grade lithium directly, conflicting with EU Battery Passport mandates

comparisonMetrics.technologyMaturity: TRL 8 (Commercial plant operational in Lyon, France)
comparisonMetrics.patentEvidence: 7 Granted Patents across EPO, USPTO, and JPO
comparisonMetrics.strategicVerdict: Shortlist #3: Strategic stopgap; re-evaluate once hydrometallurgy achieves parity

findings.claim: Operates 15,000 t/year commercial pyrometallurgical furnace facility in Lyon.
findings.snippet: Classified industrial facility operating under approved metallurgical thermal processing regulations.

findings.claim: Cobalt and nickel recovery yield exceeds 99.0% into commercial alloy matte.
findings.source: Journal of Sustainable Materials Processing, Vol. 41
findings.snippet: Slag analysis demonstrates near-complete reduction of Co and Ni into the liquid alloy phase.

findings.claim: Novel slag extraction protocol captures >85% of lithium from smelting slag.
findings.snippet: Independent metallurgical audits show lithium slag recovery remains at 60-64%; claimed 85% yield not replicated.

findings.claim: High carbon footprint (>3.8 kg CO2/kg output) creates compliance risk under 2027 EU Battery Regulation.
findings.snippet: Thermal furnace energy demands exceed proposed European Commission scope-1 emission caps for circular battery recycling.

startups.name: DisassembLi Robotics AG
startups.headline: Computer-Vision Autonomous EV Battery Pack Disassembly & Depollution
startups.recommendation: Priority 4: Upstream dismantling partner; pair with Circura's downstream hydrometallurgy.
startups.overview: DisassembLi specializes in automated robotic unscrewing and high-voltage busbar removal for prismatic and cylindrical EV packs. While they do not recycle chemical black mass, their robotic front-end removes 90% of manual labor risks.
keyStrengths: Robotic disassembly cycle time under 12 minutes per 80 kWh pack
Integrated thermal runaway vision sensors and automated water-mist quench
Strong patent position in adaptive robotic toolpath generation
keyRisks: Does not solve chemical extraction; requires pairing with chemical recycler
Only lab-validated (TRL 5) on 3 specific OEM pack architectures

comparisonMetrics.commercialDeployment: Validation cell at Swiss National Innovation Park
comparisonMetrics.strategicVerdict: Shortlist #4: Evaluate as modular pre-processing component

findings.claim: Autonomous disassembly of 80 kWh battery pack in under 12 minutes.
findings.source: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (2024)
findings.snippet: Experimental cell achieved robotic screw removal and cover separation in 11 minutes 45 seconds.

findings.claim: Compatible with all 2024 production EV pack architectures without retraining.
findings.snippet: Brochure asserts zero-shot CAD transfer learning; tested in reality on only 3 pack geometry types.

findings.claim: Will reach TRL 7 industrial pilot readiness by Q3 2027.
findings.snippet: Estimated timeline based on historical hardware-robotics development cadence and current grant funding burn.

startups.name: BioLeach Recovery Labs
startups.headline: Microbial Bio-Hydrometallurgical Extraction for Battery Scrap
startups.recommendation: Priority 5: Long-term scientific exploration; disqualified for near-term 2027 production roadmap.
startups.overview: BioLeach uses genetically optimized acidophilic bacteria (Acidithiobacillus) to bio-leach nickel, cobalt, and lithium at room temperature without synthetic acids. Extremely low energy footprint, but slow kinetics (72-hour batch times).
keyStrengths: Zero synthetic acid consumption; lowest greenhouse gas footprint
High selectivity for cobalt and lithium in bioreactor broth
keyRisks: TRL 4 (50-liter benchtop fermenters only; unproven at industrial scale)
Reaction kinetics too slow (72 hrs vs. 90 minutes for chemical hydrometallurgy)

comparisonMetrics.strategicVerdict: Disqualified for 2027 commercial deployment; track academic publications

findings.claim: Bio-leaching achieves 91% lithium extraction using engineered bacterial strains at 30°C.
findings.snippet: Bacterial consortium mobilized 91.2% Li from pulverized cathode powder over a 72-hour incubation period.

findings.claim: Bacterial strains are immune to heavy metal toxicity at commercial pulp densities (>15%).
findings.snippet: Published research confirms bacterial growth inhibition occurs when copper and nickel concentrations exceed 4% pulp density.
